subject: Literacy
title: Making my own book
subtopics: Making pages with pictures and marks
objectives: Children will make a simple book with pictures and marks.
Children will share their book with a friend.
content: Choosing a topic, making pages with pictures and marks, and sharing the book with a friend.
teachingActivities: Make a model book first; let children choose their own topic; accept any picture or mark as a page; write down what children say beside their pages; celebrate every book as a real book.
learnerActivities: Make a simple book with pictures and marks and share it with a friend.
resources: Folded paper booklets of four pages
A stapler for the teacher only
assessment: Observe whether each child makes a book with at least three pages and tells a friend about one page.
expectedOutcomes: Makes a book with at least three pages.
Tells a friend about one page.

lessons.title: What is my book about?
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will choose what their book is about.
successCriteria: Says or points to their choice
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, tell a story in order and make marks and pictures.
resources: A model book called "My Favourite Things"
Picture cards: animals, food, family, toys
lessons.starter: Show the model book and say "I made a book about my favourite things. What will your book be about?"
teacherActivities: Turn the pages of the model book and say what each page shows.
Show the topic cards and ask "What is your book about?"
Talk to each child about their topic.
Write each child’s topic on a card to put in their book.
learnerActivities: Children look and name the pictures.
Child points to a topic card.
Child says a word about their topic.
Child watches and says the topic.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Turn the pages of the model book and say what each page shows. Children: Children look and name the pictures.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the topic cards and ask "What is your book about?" Children: Child points to a topic card.
Step 3. Teacher: Talk to each child about their topic. Children: Child says a word about their topic.
Step 4. Teacher: Write each child’s topic on a card to put in their book. Children: Child watches and says the topic.

practical.title: Choose a topic
steps: Write the topic on a card.
practical.safety: Accept any choice and do not hurry. Keep cards flat and supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Offer two topics and say the words with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell what they will put in the book.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Chooses a topic for their book
Says a word about their topic
lessons.conclusion: Put the topic cards in a basket and say "Tomorrow we make our books."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child what their book will be about and look for pictures at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose what their book is about" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Making the pages
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Making pages with pictures and marks
objectives: Children will make pages for their book with pictures and marks.
successCriteria: Uses pictures or marks on each page
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, tell a story in order and make marks and pictures.
lessons.starter: Show a blank booklet and say "Every page needs a picture. What will you put on page one?"
teacherActivities: Show the booklet and how to open it and turn the page.
Show how to glue a picture or draw on a page.
Ask "Tell me about your page" and write the words under it.
Let children make a second page.
learnerActivities: Children look and turn a page.
Children glue or draw on page one.
Child tells about their page.
Child makes a second page.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the booklet and how to open it and turn the page. Children: Children look and turn a page.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to glue a picture or draw on a page. Children: Children glue or draw on page one.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Tell me about your page" and write the words under it. Children: Child tells about their page.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children make a second page. Children: Child makes a second page.

practical.title: Page making
steps: Glue or draw on page one.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic glue and keep it off faces and mouths. Wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Hold the paper steady and help to glue the picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a cover with the title and a picture.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes pages with pictures or marks
lessons.conclusion: Put the books on a table to dry and say "Tomorrow more pages."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at magazines or old cards at home and cut pictures for your child’s book.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make pages for their book with pictures and marks" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The cover and the pages
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Making pages with pictures and marks
objectives: Children will finish a book with a cover and at least three pages.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, tell a story in order and make marks and pictures.
lessons.starter: Show the model book cover and say "A book has a cover and a name on it. This is the cover."
teacherActivities: Show how to draw on the cover and put a name on it.
Give each child their booklet and help them write or stick their name on the cover.
Check each book has three pages.
learnerActivities: Children look at the cover.
Child decorates the cover.
Child adds pictures or marks.
Child counts or shows their pages.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to draw on the cover and put a name on it. Children: Children look at the cover.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child their booklet and help them write or stick their name on the cover. Children: Child decorates the cover.
Step 3. Teacher: Finish pages two and three. Children: Child adds pictures or marks.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each book has three pages. Children: Child counts or shows their pages.

practical.title: Finishing the book
steps: Make a cover and finish three pages.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic materials and supervise stickers. Keep glue sticks capped.

differentiation.support: Stick a name label on the cover and let the child decorate.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a fourth page.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many pages do you have?

expectedOutcomes: Makes a book with a cover and three pages
lessons.conclusion: Staple each book for the child and say "You made a book."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at your child’s book together and ask them to tell you about each page.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "finish a book with a cover and at least three pages" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sharing my book
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will share their book with a friend.
successCriteria: Shows their book to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, tell a story in order and make marks and pictures.
lessons.starter: Hold up a finished book and say "I made this book. Would you like to see it?"
teacherActivities: Show how to share: open the book, turn a page and say "This is my dog."
Pair the children and give them time to share.
Walk round and ask each child "What is on this page?"
learnerActivities: Children look and listen.
Child shows their book to a friend.
Child tells about a page.
Child shares with a new friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to share: open the book, turn a page and say "This is my dog." Children: Children look and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Pair the children and give them time to share. Children: Child shows their book to a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk round and ask each child "What is on this page?" Children: Child tells about a page.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap partners and share again. Children: Child shares with a new friend.

practical.title: Book sharing
steps: Swap books and look at a friend’s book.
practical.safety: Remind children to hold books gently and say thank you. Supervise sharing and keep the corner tidy.

differentiation.support: Sit beside the child and point to the page together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to read their book to a younger friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Did you like your friend’s book?
questions.expected: Yes with a nod or word.

expectedOutcomes: Shares their book with a friend
lessons.conclusion: Say thank you to your friend and put the books in the book corner.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child read their book to you and to family members.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "share their book with a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 book check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child makes and shares a book.
successCriteria: Makes a book with at least three pages
Tells a friend about one page
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can handle books, tell a story in order and make marks and pictures.
lessons.starter: Say "Show me your book" and invite children to the book corner.
teacherActivities: Invite each child to show their book and tell about one page.
Ask "What did you make?" and "What is your favourite page?"
Record each child’s level and photograph the book.
learnerActivities: Child shows the book and tells about it.
Child answers with a word or point.
Children return books to the book corner.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Invite each child to show their book and tell about one page. Children: Child shows the book and tells about it.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What did you make?" and "What is your favourite page?" Children: Child answers with a word or point.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and photograph the book. Children: Children return books to the book corner.

practical.title: Book showing
steps: Invite children one at a time.
The teacher records what they say.
practical.safety: Never force a child to speak. Accept pointing and show appreciation for every book.

differentiation.support: Sit beside the child and point to the page together.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to read their book to the group.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: makes pages; completes a cover; tells a friend about one page.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Put the books in a display and clap for all authors.
lessons.homeConnection: Make small books at home from folded paper with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child makes and shares a book" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
